Oral and maxillofacial (jaw and face) surgeons have raised concerns over the shortage of specialists in northern Nigeria, calling for increased investment in local training to improve access to specialised surgical care. They warned that the region’s continued dependence on surgeons from other parts of the country could threaten the sustainability of services, particularly when visiting professionals leave without adequately trained local specialists to take over. The Dean of the Faculty of Dental Sciences at Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, and consultant oral and maxillofacial surgeon at the university’s teaching hospital, Dr Braima Ramat, raised the alarm on Friday at the biennial conference of the Nigerian Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons in Sokoto. Ramat stated that deliberate efforts are needed to train indigenous professionals to bridge the manpower gap and ensure continuity in specialist healthcare delivery. “Oral and maxillofacial surgery is still far from the people in the North. We need to train indigenous people here because most of us are from the South. If we don’t train people from this region, specialists will come, work, and leave,” he said. The specialist explained that developing local expertise would also enable experienced surgeons to transfer their knowledge and skills to younger professionals. He noted that the specialty is expanding beyond the traditional treatment of tumours, facial fractures, and other medical conditions to include aesthetic procedures. “Oral and maxillofacial surgery is an integral part of medicine and dentistry. Previously, we were largely involved in treating problems such as tumours and fractures, but in Nigeria, we are beginning to expand into aesthetics. “Our profession is growing, and I am confident that in the next two years, we will have entered new frontiers or strengthened our presence in existing areas of practice,” he added. Surgeons seek more specialist training to tackle North’s manpower shortage Uba Sani backs Tinubu, urges North to prepare for 2031 Conflicts, El Niño worsening global hunger – UN Gbotolorun noted that the biennial conference provides an opportunity for specialists across the country to share research findings, establish professional relationships, and strengthen international collaborations. Reacting to the Federal Government’s reported N70bn intervention for oral health development, Gbotolorun said oral and maxillofacial surgeons are part of the broader oral healthcare system and expect to benefit from the initiative. He, however, clarified that the specialty is distinct from general dentistry, although both professions share responsibilities in oral healthcare. He particularly highlighted the need to address noma, a devastating disease that predominantly affects children in parts of northern Nigeria. “WHO has described noma as a neglected disease. There is what we call the Noma Belt, which extends into Northern Nigeria, and we have many children suffering from this condition. “We, therefore, expect that some of the intervention funds will address these challenges. The Minister of State for Health was represented here yesterday and gave us some assignments, and we are working towards meeting the requirements to benefit from the intervention,” he said. Also speaking, Dr Henry Leonhardt, a specialist with the Maxillofacial Department of a university hospital in Dresden, Germany, advocated the adoption of advanced surgical techniques to improve treatment outcomes for patients with noma. Leonhardt said his presentations focused on adapting microsurgical tissue transfer techniques for noma patients in Nigeria and examining treatment options for temporomandibular joint fractures. He also praised Nigerian surgeons, nurses, and other healthcare workers who participated in the surgical outreach organised ahead of the conference, describing their commitment to providing free treatment to patients who could not afford surgery as inspiring. “I was amazed to see the young surgeons, nurses, and other health workers treating patients who could not afford these operations. The spirit they demonstrated was amazing,” he said. Animashaun Salman
